pr_title: [Fix #11267] Fix an error for Style/RequireOrder when modifier conditional is used between `require`
pr_body:
Fix: #11267

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].

* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/
pr_comments:
I think that this should be sorted:

```
        require 'a'
        require 'b'
        require 'c' if/unless foo
```

Everything else (standard `if/unless` block around some `require`) should be treated as a separate block. We'll also have to document this clearly in the cop description. //cc @r7kamura
Thanks for the review. I updated this PR. Added documentation on how it behaves in each case.

Sorry for my late response and thanks for the fix @ydah!

I also agree that shorthand if/else should be sorted, and standard if/else block is treated as a separated section.
As of now, bad case and good case are listed as a pair in the example section, so it would be preferable to add that in this case as well like this:


```ruby
# bad
require 'a'
require 'c' if foo
require 'b'

# good
require 'a'
require 'b'
require 'c' if foo

# bad
require 'c'
if foo
  require 'd'
  require 'b'
end
require 'a'

# good
require 'c'
if foo
  require 'b'
  require 'd'
end
require 'a'
```

@r7kamura Thanks for replying, I appreciate it!
I updated the documentation and testing.

Using the master branch did not fix the error. Error remains the same in this. 

```bash
An error occurred while Style/RequireOrder cop was inspecting /Users/marthyn/code/floryn/config/boot.rb:7:0.
undefined method `send_type?' for nil:NilClass

            break unless sibling.send_type?
                                ^^^^^^^^^^^
```

review_comments:
However, sorting these seems to make them unmodifiable in the following cases.

```ruby
require 'c'
if foo
  require 'd'
  require 'a'
end
require 'b'
```

The following is also not sorted.
```ruby
if foo
  require 'a'
  require 'd'
end
require 'b'
require 'c'
```

Also not sorted below.
```ruby
require 'b'
require 'c'
if foo
  require 'a'
  require 'd'
end
```

The one-liner modifier form looks like it can be ordering to the following.

```ruby
        require 'a'
        require 'b'
        require 'c' if foo
```

So, I think this respects cop's intentions better.

What should we do in the following cases?
Should it be only for modifier conditional?

```ruby
require 'c'
if foo
  require 'a' if foo
end
require 'b' if foo
```
IMHO, semantically both could be treated if the branch body is just only `require`s.
